system.name: LITcoder
system.one_liner: An open-source library with a modular pipeline for building, benchmarking and comparing neural encoding models that predict fMRI responses to language.

content.variant_note: four numbered stages plus an unnumbered system-wide logger in five dashed panels; each stage is a titled panel with inputs, a pink-headed class card listing its options and a grey box with the data it returns
content.argues: Brain data and language stimuli can be turned into comparable encoding models by a fixed chain of configurable modules (assemble, extract, downsample, map), all logged in one place.
content.subject: The architecture of the LITcoder library: its four pipeline stages as class cards with options, one toy sentence carried through them, and the logger.

elements.name: fMRI / Transcripts / Timestamps
elements.role: inputs of stage 1: functional MRI data, aligned transcripts and timestamps
elements.drawn_as: three captioned icons (pink brain, document with a pencil, stopwatch) joined by lines into one arrow

elements.name: class AssemblyGenerator()
elements.role: aligns BIDS fMRI with transcripts into time-locked brain-stimulus pairs in volume or surface space
elements.drawn_as: pink-headed rounded card with parameter lines: dataset: Lebel | Narratives | LPP; data_space: Volume | Surface; atlas: LanA | Glasser | fullbrain; subject; context_length; context_type: Full | half | reset

elements.name: Aligned Data
elements.role: the stage-1 output: time-locked brain-stimulus pairs, stimulus times and TR times
elements.drawn_as: grey rounded box with a bold title and three bullets

elements.name: stimulus sentence '... he went to the store to get a cup of coffee. ...'
elements.role: a text stimulus (or an audio file, marked Or); coloured underlines of growing length show context windows
elements.drawn_as: bold text line with a lilac and pink highlight on the first words, staggered coloured underlines and the label context length, an audio-file icon and the word Or above it

elements.name: class FeatureExtractor()
elements.role: turns the aligned stimuli into features, from baselines to GPT-2 and Whisper
elements.drawn_as: pink-headed card with model_name: gpt2 | whisper | glove | wordrate and layer: Int

elements.name: word feature vectors (the, store, to, get, a, cup; 1xm)
elements.role: one 1 x m feature vector per word
elements.drawn_as: word chips (blue for the first three, green for the last three) over tall columns of empty cells, each captioned 1xm, in a grey rounded box

elements.name: TR_n / TR_n+1
elements.role: two fMRI acquisition timepoints (TR = repetition time) into which the words fall
elements.drawn_as: a blue chip and a green chip above the Downsampler card, black bars under the first three and the last three words

elements.name: class Downsampler()
elements.role: aggregates the word features to TR resolution by pooling or filtering
elements.drawn_as: pink-headed card with filter_type: Lanczos | Average | Sum | Last token; tr_times: List; stimulus_times: List

elements.name: TR-matched vectors (1, m)
elements.drawn_as: two tall cell columns with a blue and a green outline in a grey rounded box, captioned (1, m)

elements.name: FIR()
elements.role: finite impulse response expansion that adds lagged copies of the features
elements.drawn_as: label on an arrow from a column of red cells to a fanned stack of shifted red columns

elements.name: expanded features (n, m x FIR)
elements.role: the design matrix passed to Mapping
elements.drawn_as: stack of four offset columns of red-outlined cells, captioned (n, m x FIR)

elements.name: class Mapping()
elements.role: fits ridge regression with cross-validation and returns voxel or vertex predictivity
elements.drawn_as: pink-headed card with features: np.array(); targets: np.array(); folding_type: kfold | kfold_trimmed; normalize_features: bool; normalize_targets: bool; single_alpha: true

elements.name: Real / Predicted with Pearson correlation
elements.role: evaluation: real and predicted responses compared by Pearson correlation
elements.drawn_as: grey rounded box with two small line plots titled Real and Predicted, a double-headed arrow between them, italic 'Pearson correlation' and two brain renders with green arrows up to the plots

elements.name: class Logger()
elements.role: monitors all stages and writes to several backends in several runtimes
elements.drawn_as: pink-headed card with backend: W&B | TensorBoard | CSV/JSON and Runtimes: Local | HPC/SLURM

content.reading_order: Starts at panel 1 top-left (inputs, AssemblyGenerator card, Aligned Data), then panels 2 and 3 along the top row, each read top-down, then the logger panel at the lower left and panel 4 along the bottom right from FIR to the real and predicted brain responses.

layout.arrangement_note: Five dashed rounded panels in a 3 + 2 grid on white: the top row holds the numbered stages 1 to 3, the bottom row a narrow System-wide logger panel at the left and the wide stage 4 at the right. Inside each stage the flow is top-down: title, inputs or drawings, an arrow to a pink-headed class card listing its options, an arrow to the data it returns in a grey rounded box; stage 4 runs left to right instead.

lessons.what_to_learn: For a library, give every stage the same panel template: a numbered title, inputs, an arrow to a card that names the class and lists its options with vertical bars, and a grey box with the data it returns; carry one toy sentence through the stages so the data shapes are visible.
lessons.suits: Software libraries and benchmarking toolkits with a fixed pipeline of configurable modules, where the figure must show both the data flow and the available options.

evidence: AssemblyGenerator aligns BIDS fMRI with transcripts in volume or surface space
Downsampler aggregates those features to TR resolution
All stages are monitored using the Logger

summary: LITcoder is an open-source library for building and comparing neural encoding models of fMRI responses to language. Figure 1 shows its architecture as five dashed panels in a 3 + 2 grid. Stages 1 to 4 follow one template: a numbered title, inputs, an arrow to a pink-headed class card that lists the options of that module, and an arrow to the data it returns. AssemblyGenerator aligns fMRI, transcripts and timestamps; FeatureExtractor (gpt2, whisper, glove, wordrate) turns a sentence into per-word 1 x m vectors; Downsampler pools them into TR-matched vectors; FIR expansion and Mapping predict brain responses, shown as real against predicted time series and brain maps. A system-wide Logger panel lists W&B, TensorBoard and CSV/JSON.
summary_zh: LITcoder 是构建并比较 fMRI 神经编码模型的开源库。图用五个虚线面板展示架构：数据组装、特征提取、降采样、脑响应预测与映射四步，每步都是“标题-输入-粉色类卡片-输出”模板，另有全局日志面板，末尾对比真实与预测脑响应。
notes: Prior kind stage-pipeline kept and worked-walkthrough added for the sentence carried through stages 2 and 3. Which of the three logger icons stands for which backend is not labelled, so the mapping is not certain. The paper text names the FIR step as a separate FIRExpander; the figure draws it only as a label inside panel 4.
